(Currently Amended) A system for generating a counter-stimulation in a patient suffering from RLS, the system comprising: a device configured and arranged to generate a counter-stimulation in a patient suffering from RLS, the counter-stimulation of an __amplitude, intensity, and time duration that is insufficient to wake the patient but effectively relieves RLS symptoms, or sufficient to relieve RLS symptoms and allow the patient to return to sleep__ ; a controller configured and arranged to drive the counter-stimulation generation device, the controller in communication with the counter-stimulation device; and a base configured and arranged to hold the counter-stimulation generation device adjacent to a patient, the counter-stimulation device attached to the base.

(Currently Amended) The system according to Claim 1, wherein the device comprises an __activating element selected from the group consisting of a fluid pressure applicator, a mechanical point pressure applicator, a mechanical roller, a mechanical lift, a vibration generator, a nerve stimulator, a muscle stimulator, a heater, a cooler, a chemical applicator, and a magnet__.

(Currently Amended) A method of treating RLS, the method comprising: selecting a patient experiencing RLS; stimulating a portion of the patient at an __amplitude, intensity, and duration that is insufficient to wake the patient but sufficiently effective to serve as a counter-stimulation to RLS allowing the patient to return to sleep__.

(Currently Amended) The method according to Claim 15, wherein said patient is asleep; and wherein said counter-stimulation is __not sufficient to wake the patient__.

(Currently Amended) The method according to Claim 18, wherein said counter-stimulation __is selected from the group consisting of pressure application, mechanical point pressure application, a mechanically rolling against the patient's skin, mechanically lifting at least a portion of the patient, vibration, nerve stimulation, muscle stimulation, heat, cold, chemical application, and magnetism that is insufficient to wake the patient___.
